When a process dies
column2: failed reply is sent to the sender of any transaction

column1: queued on a dead thread's todo list. The sender asserts that the
received failed reply corresponds to the head of the transaction stack.
This assert can fail if the dead thread is allowed to send outgoing
transactions when there is already a transaction on its todo list
because this new transaction can end up on the transaction stack of the
original sender. The following steps illustrate how this assertion can
fail.
1. Thread1 sends txn19 to Thread2
(T1->transaction_stack=txn19
2. Without processing todo list
(T1->todo+=txn20
3. T1 processes txn20 on its todo list
(T1->transaction_stack=txn20->txn19
4. T2 dies
column2: T2->todo cleanup attempts to send failed reply for txn19

column1: T1->transaction_stack points to txn20 -- assertion failes
Step 2. is the incorrect behavior. When there is a transaction on a
thread's todo list
column2: this thread should not be able to send any outgoing

column1: synchronous transactions. Only the head of the todo list needs to be
checked because only threads that are waiting for proc work can directly
receive work from another thread
column2: and no work is allowed to be queued

column1: on such a thread without waking up the thread. This patch also enforces
that a thread is not waiting for proc work when a work is directly
enqueued to its todo list.
